description: The AWS Command Line Interface is a unified tool to manage your AWS services.
help_usage: Use *aws command help* for information on a specific command. Use *aws help topics* to view a list of available help topics. The synopsis for each command shows its parameters and their usage. Optional parameters are shown in square brackets.

endpoint-url.help: Override command's default URL with the given URL.

no-verify-ssl.help: By default, the AWS CLI uses SSL when communicating with AWS services. For each SSL connection, the AWS CLI will verify SSL certificates. This option overrides the default behavior of verifying SSL certificates.

no-paginate.help: Disable automatic pagination. If automatic pagination is disabled, the AWS CLI will only make one call, for the first page of results.

query.help: A JMESPath query to use in filtering the response data.

profile.help: Use a specific profile from your credential file.

region.help: The region to use. Overrides config/env settings.

no-sign-request.help: Do not sign requests. Credentials will not be loaded if this argument is provided.

ca-bundle.help: The CA certificate bundle to use when verifying SSL certificates. Overrides config/env settings.

cli-read-timeout.help: The maximum socket read time in seconds. If the value is set to 0, the socket read will be blocking and not timeout. The default value is 60 seconds.

cli-connect-timeout.help: The maximum socket connect time in seconds. If the value is set to 0, the socket connect will be blocking and not timeout. The default value is 60 seconds.

cli-binary-format.help: The formatting style to be used for binary blobs. The default format is base64. The base64 format expects binary blobs to be provided as a base64 encoded string. The raw-in-base64-out format preserves compatibility with AWS CLI V1 behavior and binary values must be passed literally. When providing contents from a file that map to a binary blob ``fileb://`` will always be treated as binary and use the file contents directly regardless of the ``cli-binary-format`` setting. When using ``file://`` the file contents will need to properly formatted for the configured ``cli-binary-format``.

no-cli-auto-prompt.help: Disable automatically prompt for CLI input parameters.

cli-error-format.help: The formatting style for error output. By default, errors are displayed in enhanced format.

cli-dry-run.help: Validate the command and build the request for a single AWS API operation, print it, and exit without signing or sending it. The request is printed as JSON along with ExpectedOutput, the output a successful call would produce. Options such as --query and --output apply to ExpectedOutput, which is generated from placeholder response values. JSON and YAML output is shown as data, text output as a list of rows of columns, table output as a list of lines, and it is null if nothing would be printed. This is unrelated to the operation-level --dry-run parameter some services provide, which is sent to the service. High-level and custom commands (for example aws s3 cp) are not supported; use their own options such as --dryrun. Parameter values that are modeled as sensitive, or whose names indicate a secret such as a password or token, are redacted. The request is shown before signing and before endpoint discovery, so for services that use endpoint discovery the URL can differ from the one used. Presigned URLs that would be included in the request are not generated.
